title: Tracking Protein Motions using Serial Femtosecond Crystallography with X‐Ray Free‐Electron Laser
author: Mizohata, Nango, et al.
materials: Sodium acetate trihydrate (Wako Pure Chemical Industries, 198‐01055)

This crystallization protocol is based on the method for obtaining micron‐sized crystals reported previously (Falkner et al., 2005). Whereas lysozyme typically crystallizes between pH 4 and 5, microcrystals of lysozyme can be produced with a precipitant buffer of pH 3.0. Crystals form instantaneously when a precipitant and a lysozyme solution are mixed. It is possible to vary the size of the crystal by changing the temperature (Nango et al., 2015). Lysozyme tends to form smaller crystals at lower temperatures. Here, we will explain how to prepare 5‐µm lysozyme microcrystals by fixing the temperature at 17°C.

steps.title: Prepare lysozyme microcrystals (5 µm)
steps.instruction: Make a precipitant buffer at pH 3.0, prepare a lysozyme solution, then mix the precipitant with the lysozyme solution; crystals appear instantly. Keep the mixture at 17 °C to obtain ~5 µm lysozyme microcrystals.

steps.title: Soak P450nor crystals with caged‑NO
steps.instruction: Under red light, incubate P450nor microcrystals in a solution containing the caged nitric‑oxide donor N,N'‑bis‑(carboxymethyl)‑N,N'‑dinitroso‑p‑phenylenediamine and NADH to generate TR‑SFX samples.

substeps.instruction: Perform all handling under red light
Prepare soaking solution with the caged‑NO donor and NADH
Add P450nor microcrystals to the soaking solution
Incubate for the required time (duration not specified in source)
